concepts.title: Understanding Markets
concepts.definition: A market is any arrangement where buyers and sellers meet to exchange goods and services at agreed prices; Adam Smith saw prosperity flow from markets, since people can obtain what they cannot make themselves.
concepts.key_idea: Markets turn strangers into partners: price and exchange let each person's skill serve everyone.

concepts.title: Many Kinds of Markets
concepts.definition: Markets come in many shapes: weekly haats, neighbourhood kirana shops, malls, online platforms, and wholesale mandis; each differs in scale, goods and the distance between producer and buyer.
concepts.key_idea: Same work, many forms: every kind of market matches buyers and sellers in its own way.

concepts.title: The Chain of Markets
concepts.definition: Goods travel through a chain of markets: the producer sells to a wholesaler, the wholesaler to retailers, and retailers to consumers, each link adding transport, storage and a margin to the price.
concepts.key_idea: Every hand in the chain earns and adds cost: knowing the chain explains why prices differ from farm-gate rates.

concepts.title: Being a Smart Consumer
concepts.definition: Buyers must stay alert: check labels, dates and quality marks, compare prices, and use the BEE star ratings on electronic devices to weigh running cost, not just the sticker price.
concepts.key_idea: An informed buyer disciplines the market: careful comparison rewards fair sellers and squeezes out poor goods.
